calibration.evidence: D1 describes equal-attention branching marks; D3 describes repetitive radial spikes.
calibration.refinement: Measure thumbnail readability and localized edge energy, not just vegetation coverage.

calibration.evidence: D2 explicitly contrasts connected light/shadow bands with flat ochre plus dark outlines.
D4 identifies the exclusion-mask stage and mismatched plant bases; proposes a shared field.
D1/D3 identify curved groups and directional flow, but do not explicitly diagnose the absence of broad height envelopes.
calibration.missedWhy: The first reading emphasized silhouette rhythm and tonal flow more than the distinction between apparent rolling color and actual low canopy relief.
calibration.refinement: Test real intermediate canopy relief/parallax separately from material-only suggestions of relief.

calibration.evidence: D5 compares soft sky decisions against hard, equally detailed terrestrial marks.

additionalLimits: The diagnosis was not formally blinded because the full prompt arrived together. The freeze demonstrates ordering of saved analysis and calibration, not absence of prior exposure.

grammar.relationship: A few connected lit and shaded regions should explain the field before individual plants can be seen.
grammar.observableGoal: At 160x90, the land remains legible as a framed opening and broad meadow masses; dark marks do not fragment it into static.

grammar.relationship: Clumps overlap into elongated, irregular sweeps; their height and lean vary more slowly than their edge detail.
grammar.observableGoal: At 640x360, groups have coherent crests and gaps without identical round pillows, planting rows or isolated debris.

grammar.relationship: Fine blades support close silhouettes, selected crests and focal accents; their contrast and prevalence diminish with distance.
grammar.observableGoal: A detail crop can reveal grass while the thumbnail does not depend on resolving those blades.

grammar.relationship: Substrate, plant bases and short growth sample a common world-space palette; tips separate gently through value and light.
grammar.observableGoal: Sparse areas remain grassland rather than an unrelated brown material surrounded by objects.

grammar.relationship: Exposed earth, shortened growth and mature grass overlap through gradual spatial transitions rather than a binary clearing mask.
grammar.observableGoal: The encounter opening is readable without an obvious oval exclusion boundary or black outlines at every root.

grammar.relationship: Keep the existing physical sun and tree shadows; coordinate supplementary broad world-space light variation across ground and grass.
grammar.observableGoal: Warm middle-distance accents and cooler framing remain textured and readable, without global yellow tint or black plant bases.

grammar.relationship: Near silhouettes receive most geometric detail; middle distance is grouped; the far field becomes quiet color and low-contrast shape.
grammar.observableGoal: Detail/contrast step down continuously, without visible distance bands or equally sharp marks at the horizon.

grammar.relationship: Related directional flow unifies groups while irregular crest height and local edge breakup prevent a repeated template.
grammar.observableGoal: Avoid radial agave-like tufts, hedge pillows, scalloped rows and mechanically identical wave crests.

grammar.relationship: Keep an open, dry-grass savanna with scattered existing acacias; variation reflects patches and gradual conditions rather than arbitrary decoration.
grammar.observableGoal: No new species, flowers, paths, props or dense forest are introduced to disguise grass failures.

grammar.relationship: The land should share the sky's broad shape decisions and selective edges while retaining different material character.
grammar.observableGoal: Compare reference-calibrated edge/contrast at several scales; neither maximal sharpness nor minimal detail is an aesthetic objective by itself.

reuse: Apply these relationships to future biomes by changing ecological forms and palette, not by copying fixed density or color constants.
